'''James Ellis Colliander''' (born 22 June 1967) is an American-[[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]]. He is currently Professor of Mathematics at [[University of British Columbia]] and served as Director of the [[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences]] (PIMS) during 2016-2021. He was born in [[El Paso, Texas]], and lived there until age 8 and then moved to [[Hastings, Minnesota]]. He graduated from [[Macalester College]] in 1989. He worked for two years at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] on [[fiber optic sensor]]s and then went to graduate school to study mathematics. He received his PhD from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1997 and was advised by [[Jean Bourgain]]. Colliander was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and spent semesters at the University of Chicago, the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]].

==Research==
Colliander's research mostly addresses dynamical aspects of solutions of Hamiltonian [[partial differential equations]], especially [[non-linear Schrödinger equation]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Colliander|Keel|Staffilani|Takaoka|2008}}; {{harvtxt|Colliander|Keel|Staffilani|Takaoka|2010}}.</ref>

Colliander is a collaborator with Markus Keel, [[Gigliola Staffilani]], Hideo Takaoka, and [[Terence Tao]], forming a group known as the "I-team".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1963|title=Quello Che Si Far per Amore? Della Matematica|date=18 March 2012|department=Careers in the Math Sciences|first=Gigliola|last=Staffilani|access-date=2 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180401065345/http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1963|archive-date=1 April 2018|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="tao1">{{citation|contribution-url=http://www.icm2006.org/proceedings/Vol_I/7.pdf|title=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|year=2006|contribution=The work of Terence Tao|first=Charles|last=Fefferman|authorlink=Charles Fefferman|access-date=2 January 2015|archive-date=9 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809081829/http://www.icm2006.org/proceedings/Vol_I/7.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref> The name of this group has been said to come from a mollification [[Operator (mathematics)|operator]] used in the team's ''method of almost conserved quantities'',<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120925081237/http://wiki.math.toronto.edu/DispersiveWiki/index.php/I-method I-method], Dispersive Wiki, retrieved 2015-01-02.</ref> or as an abbreviation for "interaction", referring both to the teamwork of the group and to the interactions of light waves with each other.<ref name="tao2">[http://www.icm2006.org/dailynews/fields_tao_info_en.pdf Fields Medal announcement for Terry Tao] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303230201/http://www.icm2006.org/dailynews/fields_tao_info_en.pdf |date=3 March 2016 }}, [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], 2006, retrieved 2015-01-02.</ref> The group's work was featured in the 2006 [[Fields Medal]] citations for group member Tao.<ref name="tao1"/><ref name="tao2"/>

==Organization creation==

Colliander is co-founder of the education technology company called [https://crowdmark.com Crowdmark].

Colliander, with colleagues from PIMS, created [https://syzygy.ca/ Syzygy], a project that provides interactive computing for students and teachers at universities across Canada. Syzygy operates on infrastructure provided by Compute Canada. 

Colliander, with colleagues from PIMS and [[Cybera]], created [https://callysto.ca Callysto], a project designed to improve computational thinking for students and teachers in grades 5-12.

Colliander is co-founder of the [https://2i2c.org International Interactive Computing Collaboration (2i2c)].

==Major publications==
* Colliander, J.; Keel, M.; Staffilani, G.; Takaoka, H.; Tao, T. Global well-posedness for Schrödinger equations with derivative. SIAM J. Math. Anal. 33 (2001), no. 3, 649–669.
* Colliander, J.; Keel, M.; Staffilani, G.; Takaoka, H.; Tao, T. A refined global well-posedness result for Schrödinger equations with derivative. SIAM J. Math. Anal. 34 (2002), no. 1, 64–86.
* Colliander, J.; Keel, M.; Staffilani, G.; Takaoka, H.; Tao, T. Almost conservation laws and global rough solutions to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Math. Res. Lett. 9 (2002), no. 5-6, 659–682.
* Christ, Michael; Colliander, James; Tao, Terence. Asymptotics, frequency modulation, and low regularity ill-posedness for canonical defocusing equations. Amer. J. Math. 125 (2003), no. 6, 1235–1293. 
* Colliander, J.; Keel, M.; Staffilani, G.; Takaoka, H.; Tao, T. Sharp global well-posedness for KdV and modified KdV on <math>\mathbb{R}</math> and <math>\mathbb{T}</math>. J. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (2003), no. 3, 705–749.
* Colliander, J.; Keel, M.; Staffilani, G.; Takaoka, H.; Tao, T. Multilinear estimates for periodic KdV equations, and applications. J. Funct. Anal. 211 (2004), no. 1, 173–218.
* Colliander, J.; Keel, M.; Staffilani, G.; Takaoka, H.; Tao, T. Global existence and scattering for rough solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger equation on <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math>. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 57 (2004), no. 8, 987–1014.

*{{citation |last1=Colliander |first1=J. |last2=Keel |first2=M. |last3=Staffilani |first3=G. |author3-link=Gigliola Staffilani |last4=Takaoka |first4=H. |last5=Tao |first5=T. |author5-link=Terence Tao |doi=10.1007/s00222-010-0242-2 |issue=1 |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |mr=2651381 |pages=39–113 |title=Transfer of energy to high frequencies in the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation |volume=181 |year=2010|doi-access=free |bibcode=2010InMat.181...39C |hdl=1721.1/71665 |hdl-access=free }}.
